title: What are Variables?
overview: Variables are containers used to store data values in JavaScript. They allow developers to save and reuse information throughout an application.

title: Declaring Variables
overview: JavaScript provides three keywords to declare variables: var, let, and const. Each keyword has different behavior and usage.

example.title: Variable Declaration

title: Difference Between var, let, and const
overview: var is the older way of declaring variables, while let and const were introduced in ES6. Modern JavaScript mostly uses let and const because they provide better scope control.

example.title: Comparison

title: Primitive Data Types
overview: Primitive data types store simple values directly. JavaScript has several primitive types including string, number, boolean, undefined, null, bigint, and symbol.

example.title: Primitive Types
example.content:
String: 'Hello'
Number: 100
Boolean: true
Undefined: undefined
Null: null

title: Non-Primitive Data Types
overview: Non-primitive data types store collections of data and more complex values. Objects and arrays are commonly used non-primitive types.

example.title: Object and Array

title: Type Checking with typeof
overview: The typeof operator is used to check the data type of a JavaScript value. It returns the type as a string.

example.title: typeof Example

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned about variables, variable declarations, differences between var, let, and const, primitive and non-primitive data types, and checking types using typeof.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
